category_title: Students who engage in disruptive behavior to escape or avoid writing tasks
minimal_context: Benjamin is sitting at his desk during independent work time to write a topic sentence and a detail sentence.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent work. Please write your topic sentence first, and then write your detail sentence.

STUDENT: Did you know Batman has a new car? It goes super fast! I want a car like that when I grow up.

TUTOR: We need to work on writing right now. Go ahead and start.

STUDENT: I don't know what a topic sentence is. I can't spell any of these words. Did you know Superman can fly around the whole world in one minute?

TUTOR: Just try your best to write one sentence on your paper.

STUDENT: (Pushes the paper off the desk) I'm not doing this! I don't know how to do it and I'm not writing anything!

options.A: Move Benjamin beyond his anxiety about penmanship to caring about the content of his writing.
options.B: Create a writing community founded on respect for choice and individual perspectives during independent work.
options.C: Use a digital application to take notes, organize his work, and archive past writing projects.
options.D: Provide a less frequent schedule of breaks intermittently during independent work time.
